items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: Lee Young was on my first record session.

ctx.x: Yes, I work with the same. Well, I work with either Billy Hadnott, who was on my very first record date, and he's still around, a very wonderful bass player. And then Benny Booker, who was the first bass player who went on the road with me. He went -- he was on the road with me about, I guess, a couple of years before -- before George Duvivier was

with me. George Duvivier went to Europe with me. Then I use -- right now I'm using a very fine drummer, Gene Washington. He's a very good drummer. And I have worked with -- I've worked with many drummers. Al Bartee and some of the other fine drummers around town. And, as I think I told you, Lee Young was on my first record session. He was on the, "Hurry On Down," session. At that time he was a playing musician. But now he's an executive, now.

items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: like "Hurry on Down" and "Brown Frame" and all of those things, I did with Nellie Lutcher.

ctx.x: This is one that has been published? Or one they made up for you?

No, it was published, because they gave me that thing in 1954, the first time we were over there, and I was really amazed, you know, because I had done a lot of recording with different vocalists -- because you know, like "Hurry on Down" and "Brown Frame" and all of those things, I did with Nellie Lutcher.
